title: Where Small Mistakes Matter: Quantifying State Criticality for Imitation Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.17709v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Imitation learning typically treats every demonstration state as equally important, optimizing a behavior-cloning objective uniformly across the dataset. Yet not all states are created equal: in a small number of critical states, even a slight deviation from the expert action can lead to a failure, while in many other states such errors are recoverable and inconsequential. We formalize state criticality in imitation learning as the worst-case degradation in downstream value induced by a bounded perturbation of the expert action at a given state. We then propose SCRIM, a practical State CRIticality Measure that estimates this quantity by training an adversarial disturbance policy and a value critic around a fixed imitation policy. SCRIM assigns each demonstration state a score reflecting how vulnerable the task outcome is to small, policy-relevant action errors. We show that these scores can be used to reweight behavior-cloning losses,

translated_title: 小错误在哪里至关重要：量化模仿学习中的状态临界性
translated_abstract: 模仿学习通常将每个示范状态视为同等重要，在整个数据集上均匀地优化行为克隆目标。然而，并非所有状态都是平等的：在少数关键状态中，即使与专家动作存在轻微偏差也可能导致失败，而在许多其他状态中，这类错误是可恢复且无关紧要的。我们将模仿学习中的状态临界性形式化为：在给定状态下，对专家动作施加有界扰动所导致的下游价值的最大退化。随后，我们提出SCRIM，一种实用的状态临界性度量，通过围绕固定的模仿策略训练对抗性扰动策略和价值评论家来估计这一量。SCRIM为每个示范状态分配一个分数，反映任务结果对微小的、与策略相关的动作错误的脆弱程度。我们证明这些分数可用于对行为克隆损失进行重新加权……
tldr: 本文提出SCRIM方法，通过训练对抗性扰动策略和价值评论家来量化模仿学习中各状态的关键程度，并利用所得分数重新加权行为克隆损失，使模型重点关注那些小错误即会导致失败的关键状态。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SCRIM, a practical state criticality measure that quantifies how vulnerable task outcomes are to small, policy-relevant action errors by training an adversarial disturbance policy and a value critic around a fixed imitation policy, and uses these scores to reweight behavior-cloning losses.
